items.title: #569: Connecting Agents to Data via MCP, CLI, and More
items.summary: Should your agent call an MCP server or just run a CLI? Pamela Fox joins us to share how she thinks about connecting AI and her data. She’s taught MCP workshops from PyCon to WeAreDevelopers. And, every week, an agent combs her Gmail, Outlook, and X history to build her news roundup. She uses MCP all day. Yet, there are still times you when to skip it. You'll hear how her colleague pitted the GitHub CLI against the GitHub MCP server on a real bug fix. The CLI used fewer tokens. It succeeded more often. So do we choose CLIs, MCPs, or even just APIs for connecting our agents to our data and services? Let's find out. items.title: Multi-Cloud LLM Routing and Context-Aware Coding Agents
items.summary: In this episode, we sit down with Matt Carey and Scott Crooks , engineers at Cloudflare and Miro , to look at how two very different companies are building their own AI software factories, and what happens to engineering when the code mostly writes and reviews itself. We start with the AI gateway: why a model call is no longer simple when the same model is served across multiple regions, multiple clouds, and direct from the provider, and how Miro pools rate limits and data residency rules (like EU-only models for German customers) into a single routing layer that also powers Miro’s Sidekicks. Matt walks through Cloudflare’s agent stack, from the AI gateway and Agents SDK to Flue, a JavaScript agent framework from the makers of Astro, and Cloudflare OS, an open source agent office suite he even runs at home for grocery shopping. The heart of the conversation is code review. Matt describes what he calls the best AI code reviewer he’s ever used, built on Flue and powered by an internal engineering codex written only for agents. Scott breaks down Miro’s three-layer setup, including Easel, a bot that reads production logs overnight and opens fix PRs before anyone wakes up, and explains why only about half of those PRs get merged, and how that signal is fed back to teach the system what people care about. Along the way, we cover agent experience as a new discipline, how open source maintainers are handling a flood of cheap AI pull requests, Astro reaching zero open issues, when companies should open source internal tools and how to retire them gracefully, plus a few hot takes on chocolate and nuts. We close on the rise of the “scholarly engineer,” and why understanding ideas may matter more than reading every line of code. items.title: How IT Leaders Get More Operational Value From Their ServiceNow Investment - with Assaf Resnick of BigPanda
items.summary: ServiceNow already anchors how large IT operations teams run their work — the opportunity is getting even more value out of that investment. In this episode, Assaf Resnick, CEO at BigPanda, explores how adding a layer of context and correlation on top of ServiceNow helps IT teams capture that additional value without replacing or rebuilding what they've already built. items.title: Interview #105 Vic Chynoweth, CEO of Tempo
items.summary: Vic Chynoweth, CEO of Tempo, breaks down why companies keep raising AI budgets they cannot tie to a return, and why 2027 budget planning is when CFOs finally say stop. He explains why lines of code and hours saved measure almost nothing once code is commoditized, how linking LLM spend to the code repository and the ticketing system let one company cut annualized AI spend from $3 million to $1 million with no loss of throughput, and why an expensive model should have to earn its place. Vic also dives into strategic drift, where AI speeds up the work but not the link between strategy and that work, and why shadow AI shows up first in credit card spend. Finally, he shares why delivery dates now move earlier instead of later, and why the winners will be the companies that know their market well enough to point fast teams of people and agents in the right direction. Finally, he shares why delivery dates now move earlier instead of later, and why the winners will be the companies that know their market well enough to point fast teams of people and agents in the right direction.
